expectations.text: Execution stops with a refusal instead of inventing work from the repo
The refusal states the skill serves OpenSpec projects only and that no active change exists
expectations.evidence: The reply only states 'no active OpenSpec change exists in this checkout or its git history/remotes' and the transcript's refusal says 'I can't complete the active OpenSpec change because this checkout has no openspec/ directory or change artifacts' — neither statement asserts that the skill serves OpenSpec projects only, only that no change was found.
expectations.rubric: The refusal must state that the skill serves OpenSpec projects only and that no active change exists under openspec/changes/. Content of the refusal is judged from the reply.

expectations.text: The refusal points at proposing a change first as the way in
expectations.evidence: The refusal states only 'Please provide or check out the intended OpenSpec change' and the final reply says 'Blocked: no active OpenSpec change exists'; neither points the user at proposing a change first (e.g. via an OpenSpec proposal/change-creation step) as the way in — it only asks the user to supply/checkout an existing change.
expectations.rubric: The refusal must point the user at proposing a change first as the way in. A content judgment on the reply, not a single fixed string.

expectations.text: No commits, branch changes, or file modifications are made
